name: Ostinato Drum Machine
note: Every drum is synthesised from Web Audio oscillators, noise and filters (no samples) and scheduled with the lookahead pattern: a 25 ms timer books each step 100 ms ahead at an exact AudioContext time while a rAF loop only paints the playhead from a note queue. The voice waveform is rendered by an OfflineAudioContext running the same voice code; Euclidean fills, swing, tap tempo, pattern queuing at bar end, and the clock pauses off screen. Set --acr-beats-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Typecase Font Pairing
note: System fonts only: every stack is probed with canvas measureText against a fallback, so the list says which face is installed and what it falls back to, and the same canvas measures x-height per em to judge a pairing. The modular scale is written as clamp() steps — cqi-based in the preview pane, vw-based in the exported CSS — and a live meter counts characters per line from the real paragraph width. Set --acr-type-h to 100dvh in an app.

The Tideline ReviewNo. 47 · Autumn 2026

Field notes

The last ferry to Saltmarsh Point keeps its own time

For ninety-one years the Margery Ann has crossed the estuary four times a day. Her timetable has never once been printed.

By Ines Okafor · Photographs by Tomás Lindqvist · 12 min read

At ten past six the harbour master chalks the first crossing on a slate by the slipway, and by half past the regulars are already on the bench: two nurses heading for the early shift, a man with a crate of lobster pots, a schoolgirl revising French verbs under her breath. Nobody checks a phone. The tide decides when the boat can leave the mudflats, and the tide is written down by hand.

“The tide decides. We only write it down afterwards.”

A schedule written in chalk

Four crossings a day, every day of the year, would make 1,460 sailings. Fog took 23 days in 2025, which leaves 1,368 — and 38,960 passengers, an average of 28 on each trip across the grey water.
